macro_regime: BOJ normalization (policy rate 1.0%, hawkish dissent) + intervention-backed yen stabilization + governance re-rating, versus an extended relative-price starting point
thesis_summary: Long EWJ vs short EFA. The BOJ is mid-hiking cycle (1.0% after a June hike, July hold passed only 8-1 with Takata dissenting for 1.25%, guidance flagging core inflation 'clearly above 2%' from H2 FY26) while the ECB/EAFE bloc is on hold — that rate-path divergence plus MOF's demonstrated intervention line (~164) puts a floor under the yen and supports EWJ in USD terms. FY26 GDP was upgraded to ~0.8% and the governance/buyback bid remains structural. The honest caveats: the EWJ/EFA ratio is already at the 82nd percentile of its 52-week range, foreign investors were net sellers (-¥392.5bn, week ending Aug 1), and core-core CPI softened to 1.7% — this is a trend-continuation trade, not a valuation layup.
thesis_detail: Data as of 2026-08-07 close. EWJ 96.88 (+1.82% Fri), EFA 108.55 (+1.11%), USDJPY 157.74. EWJ/EFA ratio 0.8927 — 82.5th percentile of the 52w range (0.8423–0.9272), above the 200dma (0.8781), roughly at the 50dma (0.8943); ratio +4.4% over 12m, -0.8% over 1m, so the pair has consolidated for a month after a strong run rather than extended further. Policy: BOJ hiked to 1.0% in June (first since December), held July 31 by 8-1 with Takata dissenting for 1.25% — the dissent and the 'clearly above 2%' core-inflation language keep September live; each hike widens the policy gap vs the ECB and compresses the case for new yen shorts. Yen: USDJPY peaked at 163.86 (52w high), MOF intervened late July, spot now 157.74 (-2.95% 1m). Tokyo has drawn a line; the left tail in yen (a run to 170+) is now policy-capped, which de-risks EWJ's FX translation for USD holders. DXJ/EWJ +13.2% over 12m shows hedged Japan massively outperformed during yen weakness — if the yen regime has even shifted to sideways-to-firmer, unhedged EWJ closes that gap, a direct ratio tailwind vs EFA's ~20% Japan-diluted basket. Growth: FY26 GDP forecast upgraded to ~0.8% from 0.5%; Tankan and wage momentum support the reflation narrative. Counterweights (checked per flow discipline): foreigners net sold ¥392.5bn in the latest MOF week, core-core CPI at 1.7% (softest since Aug 2022) cuts against the BOJ's own hawkish framing, and a sharp disorderly yen spike (carry-unwind style, Aug-2024 analog) historically hits the EWJ/EFA ratio hard — that is the bear case, not the base case, because intervention and gradualism argue for an orderly path. US 10Y at 4.66% keeps the differential wide enough that rapid yen appreciation requires a Fed catalyst — watch the September FOMC as much as the BOJ.
key_data_points: EWJ/EFA ratio 0.8927, 82.5th percentile of 52w range (0.8423-0.9272), above 200dma 0.8781
BOJ policy rate 1.0% after June 2026 hike; July 31 hold passed 8-1, Takata dissented for 1.25%; BOJ sees core inflation 'clearly above 2%' from H2 FY26
USDJPY 157.74, off the 163.86 52w high after late-July MOF intervention; -2.95% over 1m, flat over 3m
Japan FY26 GDP forecast upgraded to ~0.8% from 0.5% at July BOJ meeting
Foreign investors net sold ¥392.5bn of Japanese equities in week ending Aug 1 — flows not confirming the rally
Core-core CPI (ex fresh food & energy) 1.7% y/y in June, softest since Aug 2022 — soft under the BOJ's hawkish language
US 10Y 4.66%; differential still wide, capping the pace of yen appreciation absent a Fed turn
DXJ/EWJ +13.2% over 12m — yen weakness was the drag; regime shift favors unhedged EWJ closing the gap
base_case: BOJ holds in September but signals an October/December hike; yen grinds firmer to 152-156 on intervention credibility and narrowing differentials; EWJ/EFA drifts back toward the 52w high as the FX translation tailwind and governance bid offset soft core-core prints. Ratio reaches ~0.925 (+3.6%).
bull_case: BOJ hikes in September (Takata's dissent becomes consensus) and/or the Fed cuts, USDJPY breaks below 150, foreign flows flip positive on the rate-divergence story; ratio pushes through 0.927 to new 52w highs ~0.94+ (+5-6%).
bear_case: Disorderly yen spike (carry unwind or risk-off) replays Aug 2024 — local equities fall faster than the FX gain, EWJ/EFA breaks the 200dma; alternatively core-core keeps decelerating and the BOJ blinks, removing the normalization premium. Ratio to ~0.87 or below (-2.5%).
key_risks: Sharp non-linear yen spike (carry unwind) hits Japanese equities faster than FX translation helps — Aug 2024 analog; intervention caps gradual weakness, not gap moves
Core-core CPI at 1.7% and decelerating undermines the BOJ-hike thesis; a dovish surprise unwinds the normalization premium
Foreign flows already negative (-¥392.5bn latest week) — if that accelerates, the ratio's 82nd-percentile starting point has no marginal buyer
EFA hedge is ~20% Japan — the short leg partially shorts my own long, diluting the Japan-specific expression; acceptable vs ACWI's 60%+ US beta, but noted
China slowdown spillover hits Japanese cyclicals/exporters (machinery, semis) even with a stable yen

yen_view: Sideways-to-firmer, 152-160 range: intervention line drawn near 164 caps the top, BOJ hike path and hawkish dissent bias spot lower; orderly appreciation is a modest net positive for EWJ in USD and for the ratio, a disorderly spike is the bear case
